title: Creating a Cloud Storage Decoy in GCP

blocks.text: Google Cloud Storage is an object-based storage service on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). You can create cloud storage decoys and associate file datasets. Optionally, the URLs of cloud storage decoys can be added to a landmine policy to add lures to the endpoints. Cloud storage decoys can detect the following attack paths:

blocks.item: Public: Adversaries can enumerate public cloud storage by using keywords related to an organization to find exposed cloud storage accounts on the internet in an attempt to steal sensitive data.
Private: Adversaries with compromised identities of your organization can target cloud storage accounts that are accessible via the compromised identities.

blocks.text: You can view and analyze the attack details from the Zscaler Deception dashboard.
Before creating a cloud storage decoy in GCP, ensure that you have configured the integration between GCP and Deception.
To create a cloud storage decoy:

blocks.item: Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Cloud Storage.
Click Add Decoy.
See image.
The GCP Cloud Storage drawer appears.
In the GCP Cloud Storage drawer:
Project: Select the project in which you want to create the decoy.
Name: Enter a name for the cloud storage decoy.
Description: Enter a description for the cloud storage decoy.
Region: Select the GCP region in which you want to deploy the decoy.
ACL: Choose your preferred access control list for the cloud storage decoy:
Select Public if you want the cloud storage decoy to be accessible to anyone.
Select Private if you want the cloud storage decoy to be accessible only to internal adversaries.
File Dataset: Select a file dataset that you want to be hosted within the cloud storage decoy.
See image.
Click Save.
If you want to add multiple cloud storage decoys to GCP, repeat the previous steps for each decoy and then deploy all decoys simultaneously.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings.
Locate the GCP project you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the gcp-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the gcp-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of Google Cloud Storage bucket-based Terraform back end:
{ "terraform": { "backend": { "gcs": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "prefix": "deception/terraform" } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same GCP project.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and set the user agent for Terraform:
export TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT="<value_from_ui>"
Run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed.
Run the following command to export the state file as JSON:
terraform output -json gcp_terraform_output > deployment-output.json
The JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings, locate the GCP project you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

Upon successful deployment, the cloud storage decoy is added to GCP. The deployment status is indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the cloud storage decoys table (Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Cloud Storage) within the Deception Admin Portal. To learn how to configure lures using cloud storage decoys, see Configuring Lures Using GCP Decoys.
